transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-28
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jason Muir (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Evelyn Park (Peregrine Head of Platform), Marco Ruiz (Peregrine SRE), Lena Zhao (Peregrine AI/ML Lead), Samir Patel (Peregrine Product)

Summary (auto): Kickoff to scope a 6-week POC to integrate Redwood's inference platform using OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDKs. Key emphasis on function/tool calling (structured outputs), throughput/latency benchmarks for production routing workloads, and deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private).

[00:00:00] Jason Muir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros — i'm Jason, AE on the account, Priya and Diego are our SEs. evelyn, do you want to kick off on Peregrine's side?

[00:00:14] Evelyn Park: Sure, uh hi all. we run the parcel routing and ETA systems, we're exploring LLMs to power a routing assistant for ops and a customer support agent. primary asks: high throughput during peak, strict 200ms p50-ish target for short queries, and deterministic structured output for downstream systems. We don't want hallucinations in the routing payloads.

[00:00:40] Priya Nair: Great, thanks. quick clarifying q: when you say "short queries" is that the agent prompts like single-turn API calls or multi-turn stateful conversations?

[00:00:50] Lena Zhao: Mostly single-turn enrichment calls — you send a micro-prompt with package metadata, we need a JSON back with routeId, priorityFlags, and a list of candidate carriers. sometimes there's follow-up for clarifications but the 90% path is single-turn.

[00:01:12] Marco Ruiz: On infra — we have private VPCs in GCP, prefer not to have payloads leave our VPC for PII-enriched metadata. we also have corporate KMS for keys and need SOC2 / audit proofing.

[00:01:30] Diego Ramos: Noted. we support hosted (Redwood API), dedicated pools, and private deployments (VPC/on-prem). for POC we can run hosted tests while we evaluate private connect. do you have a preferred timeline?

[00:01:42] Evelyn Park: Want to move fast — 6 weeks to prove concept, vendor decision after. main success criteria: avg latency p50 <= 200ms for 256-token effective context, p95 under 500ms; throughput target ~500 QPS at peak with batching; structured output fidelity > 98% schema compliance on our test set; cost target under our internal threshold TBD.

[00:02:10] Priya Nair: That gives us something concrete. We'll design two benchmark scenarios: one using our OpenAI-compatible hosted endpoint — quick to run; and one using a dedicated quantized model on GPU for a latency/throughput comparison. we'll measure token cost, token/sec, p50/p95, and end-to-end time including any function-calling parsing overhead.

[00:02:34] Samir Patel: How much work for our engineers to swap in an OpenAI-compatible endpoint? we have existing code that calls openai.ChatCompletion.

[00:02:41] Jason Muir: Minimal. Redwood's SDK has a drop-in OpenAI-compat layer — same request shapes, plus optional SDK helpers for structured output and tool/function calling. we also have node/python examples to demonstrate function signature binding and validation.

[00:02:58] Lena Zhao: On structured output: we will supply JSON Schema for the route object. can Redwood validate model responses against schema and surface mismatches?

[00:03:08] Priya Nair: yes — we have a structured-output verifier in the SDK that attempts a best-effort parse, returns diagnostics, and can auto-retry with pinned instructions. also we can include a reranker or a constrained decoding profile to reduce schema violations. note: constrained decoding sometimes affects latency/cost.

[00:03:34] Marco Ruiz: About function or tool calling — we want to have model suggest actions and then call internal services (eg: seat assignment, price lookup). does Redwood support the function-calling protocol?

[00:03:44] Diego Ramos: We support a function-calling surface compatible with OpenAI's format. functions are registered and the model returns a call payload; the SDK can automatically marshal that into service calls or return structured JSON for validation first.

[00:03:58] Evelyn Park: Great. security: SSO (SAML) and RBAC needed for console/ops. audit logs retained for 90 days minimum, and we need KMS integration for key custody. any caveats on private deployments?

[00:04:14] Jason Muir: For Private we offer a customer-managed control plane and option for on-prem. KMS integrations with cloud KMS and HSM are supported; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. SAML/SSO + fine-grained RBAC are standard in our dedicated/enterprise plans. noted: we'll share SOC2 docs and network allowlist ranges.

[00:04:38] Lena Zhao: For the bench, we'll provide a 48-hour traffic dump with payload sizes and QPS. what formats do you need?

[00:04:45] Priya Nair: JSON lines (timestamp, prompt, response-length estimate, context-size) is perfect. and sample golden outputs for schema checks.

[00:04:56] Jason Muir: We'll run two bench passes: 1) hosted OpenAI-compat endpoint with our standard small footprint model tuned for throughput; 2) dedicated GPU quantized variant with batching and KV cache warmed. We'll also run a cold-start simulation.

[00:05:12] Marco Ruiz: You mentioned KV cache — for single-turn calls do we still benefit?

[00:05:18] Priya Nair: For single-turn, KV cache is less helpful, but we can use prefix caching for repeated identical prompts (like standard system instruction). Batching will be the main lever for throughput. Quantization helps with instance density and cost.

[00:05:34] Samir Patel: On telemetry — we need per-route token counts and cost breakdown to align with our finance team. can Redwood expose token-level billing and per-request latency traces?

[00:05:43] Diego Ramos: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. for the POC we'll share sample dashboards and how to read them.

[00:05:55] Evelyn Park: What's the expected cost delta between hosted and dedicated for our QPS? we need a ballpark to include in internal evaluation.

[00:06:03] Jason Muir: We'll provide ranges: hosted is typically higher per-token but lower operational overhead; dedicated has fixed capacity cost but lower marginal token cost. Priya will run the bench and deliver a cost-per-1k-token estimate for both scenarios.

[00:06:18] [00:06:18] Lena Zhao: Any gotchas around OpenAI schema compatibility? we've had issues where function arg names mismatch slightly.

[00:06:27] Priya Nair: We see that. our SDK includes strict schema enforcement options and a shim that normalizes names. still good to align on JSON Schema naming conventions up front.

[00:06:40] Marco Ruiz: Network wise, for private we need VPC peering details and static IP ranges. can you provide those?

[00:06:46] Jason Muir: We'll put those in the security pack. for the POC we can run hosted benches first to avoid lengthy network provisioning, but prefer to demonstrate a private connect in the second phase.

[00:06:58] Samir Patel: Timeline check — what's realistic to get bench results back? two weeks?

[00:07:03] Priya Nair: yes, assuming Peregrine provides logs and schema by end of week. bench run + analysis ~10 business days.

[00:07:12] Evelyn Park: ok we'll try to get the logs by Monday.

[00:07:18] Jason Muir: Good. for success criteria recapping: 1) p50 <= 200ms, p95 <= 500ms for 256-token effective payloads; 2) sustain peak ~500 QPS with batching without SLA violations; 3) structured output schema compliance >= 98% on test set; 4) cost estimate within your threshold. we'll capture that in the POC doc.

[00:07:40] Lena Zhao: and we'll include a small holdout of golden examples to check for regressions.

[00:07:46] Diego Ramos: Perfect. any blockers from your side?

[00:07:50] Marco Ruiz: firewall approvals can take a week, but for hosted bench it's fine. one ask: can Redwood redact PII during logs ingestion for the bench? we can't send raw PII.

[00:07:59] Priya Nair: yes, you can sanitize logs client-side; alternately provide synthetic data that matches distribution. we can also run tests inside a private environment if needed.

[00:08:10] Samir Patel: about function calling — can Redwood surface a dry-run so we can validate actions before execution? we don't want accidental mutations.

[00:08:18] Diego Ramos: There's a dry-run mode — model returns a function call payload but not executed. you can choose to validate then execute. good for safety during integration.

[00:08:27] Evelyn Park: That eases concerns. ok, let's talk deliverables and owners —

[00:08:30] Jason Muir: i'll take the POC SOW and deck; priya will run benches. we need the logs and schema from Peregrine. diego will draft the security/network checklist.

[00:08:40] Lena Zhao: quick question on quality monitoring — can Redwood alert if schema compliance drops or hallucination rate exceeds threshold?

[00:08:47] Priya Nair: yes, Redwood Optimize can monitor prompt sets, run evals, and trigger regression alerts tied to golden prompts. we can include that in the POC scope as optional.

[00:08:58] Marco Ruiz: final Q — are there vendor lock-in concerns if we use Redwood's SDK?

[00:09:04] Jason Muir: The SDK aims to be OpenAI-compatible; we avoid lock-in by keeping request shapes standard. some Redwood-only features exist (console hooks, structured-output verifier) but you can integrate them incrementally.

[00:09:18] Samir Patel: Good. next steps recap?

[00:09:21] Jason Muir: Action items and owners we'll send in email. bench start on receipt of logs and schema. security pack and SOC2 docs shared by early next week. schedule a 30-minute VPC deep-dive once network info is ready.

[00:09:34] Evelyn Park: Sounds good. thanks everyone.

[00:09:38] Jason Muir: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes on transcript quality: some proper nouns may be mis-transcribed (e.g., KMS sometimes as K-M-S, Redwood product names occasionally shortened). There were a few crosstalk snippets that have been smoothed for readability.
